articles.title: Gujarat man burns 2-year-old son alive, buries body to destroy evidence
articles.summary: Father in Suigam accused of burning 2.5-year-old son; body buried to conceal evidence. Police exhumed remains and filed murder charges.
articles.body: PALANPUR: A man allegedly burned his two-and-a-half-year-old son alive after dousing him with petrol at Suigam in Vav-Tharad district, before burying the body at a cremation ground in an attempt to destroy evidence, police said.The killing came to light after the accused’s uncle lodged a complaint with Suigam police. The accused, Ashok Raval, allegedly considered raising his son, Navghan, a burden, as his wife had been living separately for some time.According to the complaint filed by Babu Raval, a resident of Ravalvas in Suigam, Ashok had married a woman from Himmatnagar. She had been living separately, leaving him to care for their young son alone. With no one to look after the child, Ashok found the responsibility of raising him increasingly difficult.On Oct 13, between 1pm and 2pm, Ashok allegedly poured petrol on Navghan and set him on fire. He later took the toddler to a hospital, where the child died.To conceal the circumstances of the death, Ashok, along with family members, buried the child’s body at the community burial ground rather than allowing the cause of death to come to light.Babu later learnt about the matter and approached Suigam police, filing a complaint against his nephew.Police conducted an excavation at the burial ground in the presence of officials, including the mamlatdar, and exhumed the child’s body for further investigation.Suigam police registered a case against Ashok for murder and causing disappearance of evidence.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Rajkot | Silver Rate in Rajkot | Bank Holidays in Rajkot | Public Holidays in Rajkot | Rajkot AQI | Weather in Rajkot | Petrol Price in Rajkot | Diesel Price in Rajkot | CNG Price in Rajkot | LPG Price in RajkotStay updated with the latest Rajkot news. articles.title: 'Go to jail or be shot’: Trump warns US military secret leakers
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump has a stark warning for those who leak military secrets: face jail or risk being shot.
articles.body: US President Donald Trump has a stark warning for those who leak military secrets: face jail or risk being shot. He made the remarks at a rally in Bullhead City, Arizona, on Wednesday (local time), while discussing the US bombing of Iran's nuclear facilities in June 2025.“In my opinion, leakers should be shot,” Trump said, drawing applause from the crowd. “In the old days we used to shoot leakers, you know?”The US President described the B-2 bombers used in the operation as “totally stealth” aircraft that dropped “very large bombs” on the facilities. He further claimed that someone had alerted the news media about the planned attack, adding, “They ought to go to jail or be shot,”This is not the first time Trump has threatened government sources who share information with journalists. When he first took office, he promised to track down the “low-life leakers” who provided the news media with information about his administration's ties to Russia, New York Times reported.Alyssa Farah Griffin, a White House official during Trump's first term, told a Mediaite podcast that she had heard Trump talk about executing a staff member who leaked information.Trump's remarks come as he pushes to restore the use of the federal death penalty, a move he campaigned for after the Biden administration imposed a moratorium on executions.Earlier this month, Trump approved the first legally sanctioned public execution in the US since 1936, paving the way for Nidal Malik Hasan to be killed by firing squad on December 3. Hasan, an Army psychiatrist, killed 13 fellow soldiers at Fort Hood in Texas in 2009.The Trump administration has said the execution would be streamed live. Trump later confirmed that he had “absolutely” agreed to the proposal, while acknowledging that the plan could change.“They are making a determination about that, but he will be killed,” Trump said. “I really don't care how he goes, as long as he goes.”The Pentagon had earlier indicated that the execution would be livestreamed, with US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth saying the military would ensure people could watch it. However, Vice President JD Vance expressed uncertainty over whether the broadcast would go ahead.Vance described Hasan's attack as the worst terrorist attack on American soil outside the September 11, 2001, attacks, but said he would not watch the execution if it were streamed live.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'Nobody can browbeat judiciary': SC issues notice to Rahul Gandhi, Akhilesh Yadav and others over October 12 march
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday issued notices to Rahul Gandhi, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav and other protestors over their October 12
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday issued notices to Rahul Gandhi, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav and other protestors over their October 12 march to the apex court to protest alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The bench, headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and comprising Justice Joymalya Bagchi, said issuing notice on the petition did not mean it was condoning the conduct of the political leaders during the march.ALSO READ: Imran Khan asked to leave India: What rights do OCI cardholders have?“We will issue notice but we want to know his conduct on the next date of hearing,” the CJI said, referring to Rahul.During the hearing, Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said, “We are not sitting in ivory towers, we are aware of statements made outside the Court” after lawyers referred to attempts to “browbeat” the judiciary through the march. The CJI said the court would ask Rahul to explain how crowds entered the Supreme Court premises during the demonstration.The INDIA bloc’s ‘Chalo Dilli – March for Democracy’, led by Rahul, brought thousands of supporters into central Delhi on October 12. The opposition was demanding chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation and a halt to the SIR exercise over alleged electoral irregularities.The march saw supporters gather along roads between Connaught Place and the Supreme Court, waving party flags and raising slogans. Police stopped the procession near Barakhamba Road, where some demonstrators pushed through barricades as security personnel attempted to hold them back. The crowd later gathered along Bhagwan Das Road, with some supporters climbing onto parked police vehicles and buses.Rahul was joined by Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Akhilesh Yadav, RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav and other INDIA bloc leaders. The procession followed the CJI’s refusal to meet opposition representatives seeking to submit a memorandum on alleged electoral irregularities. He had advised them to file a formal petition, citing matters already pending before the court.The opposition’s separate petition challenging the SIR process alleges arbitrary voter deletions and seeks greater transparency and safeguards in the revision of electoral rolls. The Supreme Court also issued notice to the Election Commission of India on that plea.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Demi Moore owns 2,000 dolls, including one-of-a-kind art pieces, and once planned to turn her extraordinary collection into a museum
articles.summary: Hollywood actor Demi Moore has an unusual passion that extends beyond the screen, with a collection of around 2,000 dolls, many of which she considers
articles.body: Hollywood actor Demi Moore has an unusual passion that extends beyond the screen, with a collection of around 2,000 dolls, many of which she considers contemporary works of art. Unlike conventional playthings, these pieces are hand-sculpted figures designed to capture human expressions and emotions in miniature. Moore discussed her collection in a September 2024 interview with The Guardian, revealing that she still owned the dolls but had not added to the collection for a long time. The actor had also considered turning her extraordinary assortment into a museum, an idea she discussed publicly years earlier. Her fascination began with a doll gifted by her then-husband, Bruce Willis, after the birth of their daughter, eventually growing into a collection featuring unique creations by French artist Anne Mitrani.How Demi Moore's 2,000-doll collection beganMoore traced the origins of her collection to a gift from Bruce Willis, whom she married in 1987. In a January 2025 interview with W Magazine, she recalled that she had recently given birth when Willis brought home a doll created by French artist Anne Mitrani after travelling for a film promotion trip.Their daughter was approximately a week old at the time. Moore described the doll as an introduction to a new kind of play and an experience that allowed her to explore emotion through an unexpected medium. The gift sparked an interest that gradually developed into a collection of approximately 2,000 dolls.Rather than collecting conventional toys, Moore became drawn to figures that resembled real people and conveyed distinct expressions. Over time, the collection grew to include numerous individually crafted pieces, particularly works associated with Mitrani, whose creations helped shape Moore's appreciation for art dolls.Why Moore considers her dolls works of artFor Moore, the dolls are more than decorative objects or childhood playthings. She has described them as contemporary art pieces, many of which are one-of-a-kind creations shaped by the artist's attention to human expression and detail.In her W Magazine interview, Moore discussed how the figures capture moments of emotion through their faces, poses and carefully sculpted features. Their lifelike appearance distinguishes them from mass-produced dolls, giving each piece an individual character.Mitrani's work occupies a significant place in the collection. The French artist is known for creating detailed figures that resemble miniature human beings, with an emphasis on expressions and realistic features. Moore's interest in these works reflects her appreciation for the craftsmanship involved in translating human characteristics into small sculptural forms.The museum she once wanted to establishMoore's ambition to create a museum for her dolls dates back several decades. A The Washington Post feature published on July 31, 1999, documented the collection and reported that a curator associated with the doll world had been helping organise it while travelling internationally to find additional pieces.The idea resurfaced in a 2007 feature published by Tribute magazine. Moore discussed her collection of antique dolls, many created by Mitrani, and said she was considering opening a doll museum. She also described the figures as remarkably lifelike works of art.The 2007 feature reported that individual pieces could cost as much as $20,000, highlighting the specialist market for unique art dolls. Moore also expressed the belief that her collection might be the world's largest collection of Mitrani's work.In her September 2024 interview with The Guardian, Moore returned to the museum idea, explaining that she had wanted to establish a dedicated space because some of the dolls were extraordinary works of art. The concept reflected her view that the pieces deserved to be appreciated as artistic creations rather than treated simply as personal possessions.Moore has stopped actively collecting dollsAlthough Moore confirmed in 2024 that she still owned the collection, she said she had not added to it for a long time. In her January 2025 interview with W Magazine, she also discussed having moved away from actively collecting the dolls.The collection nevertheless remains an unusual part of her personal interests. Her comments reveal a long-standing fascination with objects that inspire curiosity through their scale, craftsmanship or unexpected appearance.During her Guardian interview, Moore also spoke about collecting objects of unusual sizes, including oversized and miniature items. Among the larger pieces she mentioned were a six-foot butcher's knife, a pair of three-foot scissors, boxing gloves and a clipboard. She explained that she finds unusual scale interesting and enjoys the playful effect of seeing familiar objects transformed into something unexpected.This interest in objects that challenge ordinary expectations provides another perspective on her doll collection. Both miniatures and oversized items alter how people perceive familiar forms, drawing attention to their details and proportions.The lasting appeal of Moore's extraordinary collectionMoore's collection stands out because of its scale and the artistic character of its individual pieces. What began with a gift from Willis developed into an assortment of approximately 2,000 dolls, many associated with Mitrani's distinctive approach to sculpting lifelike figures.Her long-standing interest in creating a museum also reflects a desire to present the dolls as works of art worthy of public appreciation. Through their carefully crafted expressions and individual features, the figures occupy a space between sculpture and collectible art.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Viral  Bihar man, Russian woman’s love story turns out to be fake; here’s what actually happened
articles.summary: PATNA: A viral love story claiming that a Russian woman travelled thousands of kilometres to marry a man from a poor family in Bihar has turned out to be
articles.body: PATNA: A viral love story claiming that a Russian woman travelled thousands of kilometres to marry a man from a poor family in Bihar has turned out to be entirely fabricated, with the video actually featuring a British NGO representative visiting a village in Purnia for a social initiative.The story, which claimed that a Bhagalpur man named Rahul had fallen in love with a Russian woman called Julie while working in Russia, spread rapidly across social media. Several media platforms and local content creators amplified the claim, with videos about the alleged romance attracting millions of views. Some posts even claimed that the couple planned to marry in November 2026 with the consent of their families.However, the people featured in the video were misidentified, and the supposed international love story had no factual basis.The man in the video is Namit, a resident of Purnia district, not Rahul from Bhagalpur. The foreign woman is Andrea Connolly, who is associated with Shivia, a British non-governmental organisation. Shivia works with a local organisation, Saathi, in Purnia on initiatives aimed at helping women become self-employed.Abhishek Kumar Singh, coordinator of Saathi, said, “A six-member team of women visited Purnia on October 7 and 8 to understand the organisations’ grassroots work. Andrea was among the visitors. During the visit, local women welcomed the team with a bouquet of roses, and Andrea visited some of their homes.”Photographs of the interactions were subsequently uploaded to the organisation’s social media accounts. As the visitors moved through the village, curious residents gathered to see them. Namit was among the locals present, and someone recorded a video of the gathering.The footage was later circulated with a fabricated narrative about a romance between Namit and Andrea, falsely portraying her as a Russian woman named Julie who had travelled to Bihar to marry him. The bouquet visible in Andrea’s hands in the viral footage was the same one presented to her by the local women during the welcome.Singh said, “The women were guests of the organisation and expressed concern over the spread of the misleading video.”He said Saathi was considering legal action against those responsible for circulating the false claims.He also criticised media organisations for publishing the story without proper verification, saying the reports had damaged the reputation of the organisations involved and harmed India’s image.Attempts to contact Namit were unsuccessful, as his mobile phone was switched off.Local residents said he had never travelled abroad and had gone to a neighbouring village after learning that a group of foreign women had arrived there.It remains unclear who recorded and first circulated the video with the false claims, or whether Namit had any role in its dissemination. His possible involvement, if any, would need to be established through further inquiry.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Patna | Silver Rate in Patna | Bank Holidays in Patna | Public Holidays in Patna | Patna AQI | Weather in Patna | Petrol Price in Patna | Diesel Price in Patna | CNG Price in Patna | LPG Price in PatnaStay updated with the latest Patna news. articles.title: London’s oldest restaurant, where Edward VII met his mistresses and showbiz stars gathered backstage, has now been donated to the National Trust after 228 years
articles.summary: A 228-year-old building that houses London's oldest restaurant has been donated to Europe's biggest conservation charity in the hope of saving it for
articles.body: A 228-year-old building that houses London's oldest restaurant has been donated to Europe's biggest conservation charity in the hope of saving it for centuries to come, according to a report by the Associated Press. Along with the building, the donation also includes items such as visitor books, menus, caricatures, photographs, stained glass and signs. It also includes annual rent from the ongoing restaurant business, which will go into conservation work each year.A memorable pastThe move, which now ensures that the Covent Garden restaurant cannot be sold on, has drawn attention for more than just its history. According to a report by Daily Mail, Edward VII often dined there with actress Lillie Langtry, even having a curtain specially installed to maintain their privacy. The king, who ruled from 1901 until his death nine years later, was married to Princess Alexandra of Denmark, with whom he had six children. However, he was known to have had a series of affairs. Among the women romantically linked with him were Lady Randolph Churchill, Winston's mother, actress Sarah Bernhardt, singer Hortense Schneider and socialite Alice Keppel.Apart from the royalty, a slew of celebrities frequented the eatery. Author Charles Dickens, rock star David Bowie, the Beatles' manager Brian Epstein, Charlie Chaplin, Carol Channing and many others were spotted there. Authors William Makepeace Thackeray, H. G. Wells, Evelyn Waugh, John Le Carré, as well as agony aunt Claire Rayner have dined there. James Bond actors Roger Moore, Timothy Dalton and Pierce Brosnan have also been there.Rules introduced the popular Royal 29 cocktail in the honour of the marriage of William and Kate on April 29, 2011. The cocktail included ground rose petals and crystallised violet petals, citrus juice, a shot of No. 3 Gin from Berry Bros & Rudd, half a shot of Lillet, a single measure of pink vodka and a Maraschino cherry.Along with this, Rules has an eccentric 'green room' story. The venue's website calls it 'an unofficial "green room" for the entertainment industry, hosting legendary actors from Henry Irving to Laurence Olivier and cinema icons like Buster Keaton and Charlie Chaplin'.Ownership and legacyAcross its history spanning 228 years, the restaurant has been owned by only four different families. Its latest owner, Jean Pierre Mayhew, 78, decided after more than four decades to give the £11million building housing the restaurant, between Covent Garden and The Strand in central London, to the Trust. Rules will continue to operate as before, with Ricky McMenemy, the existing owner of the catering business, becoming a commercial Trust tenant. Mayhew bought the restaurant in 1984 from the daughter of Tom Bell. McMenemy has worked there for 35 years, with the restaurant employing 90 staff members and accommodation for 90 diners.“There are few restaurants in the world that have endured the test of time like Rules,” Mayhew said Wednesday, as per AP. “The Trust will protect this place in a way that no one else could, safeguarding its bricks and mortar, its famous interior and its invisible atmosphere, too.”“As an independent business, it gives us both the security and peace of mind that our home will be in very good hands and be protected and secure going forward,” said McMenemy. “Having already established a very amicable working relationship with the Trust, we look forward to another two centuries in this, our home.”Rules was opened by Thomas Rule, whose family remained owners until the end of the First World War. In the beginning, the restaurant focused on oysters, which are still on the menu, now at £5.75 each. Just before World War I, Charles Rule, a descendant of the founder, considered a move to Paris, and crossed paths with Tom Bell, owner of the Parisian restaurant, Alhambra, leading to an unexpected yet transformative business exchange.Other meals which could have been enjoyed by Dickens or patrons such as Charlie Chaplin and Carol Channing have included steak and kidney pie, now £26.25, with chips, mash or dauphinoise potatoes for £6.95 extra. The puddings and cheese menu features an apple and sultana crumble with custard for £11.50, and Stilton cheese and biscuits priced at £13.95.Its website says that during the Second World War it remained open, "offering essential rationed meals at five shillings while still indulging patrons with the likes of rabbits, grouse and pheasants."It was previously threatened with destruction by the Greater London Council in 1971, set to be demolished along with nearby historic market Covent Garden, while the Strand was to become a dual carriageway. Only a campaign involving Rules diner and poet Sir John Betjeman helped stop the unwanted 'progress'. Sir John said at a planning meeting: "A place constantly used by actors, managers and famous people, as Rules has, acquires an invisible atmosphere, just as a church frequented by praying people acquires an atmosphere. We can sense it, and it will not photograph."You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: ‘He was under massive debt’: Shraddha Dubey recounts events before Lucknow bizman’s death
articles.summary: LUCKNOW: A second video statement by Shraddha Dubey, who is wanted in connection with the death of 28-year-old restaurant owner Shiva Sharma, has surfaced
articles.body: LUCKNOW: A second video statement by Shraddha Dubey, who is wanted in connection with the death of 28-year-old restaurant owner Shiva Sharma, has surfaced on social media. Police have announced a reward of Rs 25,000 for information leading to her arrest.In the video, Dubey denies any role in Sharma’s death, describes it as a suicide and claims that he was under severe financial stress due to debts of Rs 15 lakh to Rs 20 lakh. She has also appealed to the media to stop linking her to the case, saying she is under immense mental distress following the incident.Dubey says she had known Sharma for around four months and had been in a relationship with him for approximately two months. According to her, they had not spoken for several days before October 7, when Sharma allegedly contacted her driver through a tea vendor at the main crossing in Lucknow’s Kapurthala area.She claims Sharma was crying when he tried to reach her. Dubey says she called him twice before he called her around 2am and told her he was coming to meet her. He later arrived in his BMW. According to her account, he had consumed alcohol before they met.Dubey says they then went to Pedalers Cafe, where Sharma ordered matcha for her and her driver, along with juice for himself. She claims they later returned home, with Sharma driving her car and her driver driving Sharma’s BMW.Claims Sharma was under financial stressDubey alleges that Sharma had debts of Rs 15 lakh to Rs 20 lakh and frequently received calls from creditors when they were together. She claims he had told her that he might take his own life if he failed to repay the money, although she says she did not take his statements seriously at the time.Dubey says she has screenshots of their conversations that she intends to share. She also claims Sharma’s mobile phone has been handed over to the police and that an examination of his call detail records could help establish the nature of the calls he received from creditors and shed light on the circumstances leading to his death.Her claims about Sharma’s debts and state of mind have not been independently verified.Denies torture, recounts events before deathDubey denies that Sharma was subjected to torture or abuse while he was with her. She says Sharma’s friends, whom she identifies as Ashwini Mishra and Harsh, visited them on October 8 and that their interactions were normal.She also says her sister visited her home that day to discuss arrangements for Navratri. According to Dubey, her sister barely knew Sharma and had no connection with the circumstances surrounding his death.Recounting the events of October 9, Dubey says she and Sharma woke up and went to the drawing room to have tea. Sharma then went to the washroom but closed the main entrance door, which she claims was unusual.Dubey says she became suspicious because of his earlier statements about his financial difficulties and asked her sister to check on him. However, she claims Sharma jumped from the balcony before her sister could open the door.Sharma died after falling from the fourth floor of an apartment near Balu Adda in Lucknow’s Hazratganj area on October 9.Alleges Sharma’s mother assaulted her driverDubey claims Sharma’s mother arrived at the hospital after being informed of the incident and assaulted her driver. She says the incident would have been captured on hospital CCTV cameras.She further alleges that Sharma’s family accused her and others of murder without establishing the circumstances surrounding his death. Dubey says CCTV footage, call records and other evidence should be examined to determine what happened.These claims form part of Dubey’s account and have not been independently corroborated.Appeals to media, cites mental distressTowards the end of the video, Dubey appeals to the media not to circulate rumours or repeatedly link her to the murder allegations. She says her deteriorating health and mental state prevented her from speaking immediately after the incident.She adds that she is grieving the loss of someone close to her and claims that continued harassment could push her towards suicide.Police have announced a reward of Rs 25,000 each for information leading to the arrest of three people in connection with Sharma’s death: Dubey, her sister Rashmi Dubey, and Tanveer Ali, alias Danish, reportedly Dubey’s driver.The investigation into Sharma’s death is continuing. Dubey’s claims about suicide, financial distress and the events leading up to Sharma’s fall remain to be examined by investigators against CCTV footage, call detail records, witness accounts and other available evidence.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Lucknow | Silver Rate in Lucknow | Bank Holidays in Lucknow | Public Holidays in Lucknow | Lucknow AQI | Weather in Lucknow | Petrol Price in Lucknow | Diesel Price in Lucknow | CNG Price in Lucknow | LPG Price in LucknowStay updated with the latest Lucknow news. articles.title: Amelia Earhart vanished over the Pacific in 1937; a theory suggests she survived a crash landing on a remote island before giant coconut crabs consumed her remains
articles.summary: Amelia Earhart, one of the world’s most celebrated aviation pioneers, disappeared over the Pacific Ocean on July 2, 1937, while attempting to fly around
articles.body: Amelia Earhart, one of the world’s most celebrated aviation pioneers, disappeared over the Pacific Ocean on July 2, 1937, while attempting to fly around the world with navigator Fred Noonan. Nearly nine decades later, her fate remains unknown. A new 17-member expedition backed by Purdue University and the Archaeological Legacy Institute reached Nikumaroro, a remote island in the Republic of Kiribati, on October 12, 2026, to investigate an underwater object that could potentially be linked to her missing Lockheed Electra. The search has renewed attention to the long-standing theory that Earhart and Noonan may have reached the island after failing to locate Howland Island. According to this hypothesis, Earhart may have survived as a castaway before dying there, with giant coconut crabs potentially scavenging her remains and scattering her bones.The theory that Amelia Earhart survived a crash only to be eaten by giant crabsThe hypothesis, known as the Nikumaroro castaway theory, proposes that Earhart and Noonan failed to find Howland Island and instead landed on the reef surrounding Nikumaroro, then known as Gardner Island. Supporters believe the reef may have provided a rough landing surface, allowing them to survive the initial disappearance. According to this theory, Noonan eventually died, while Earhart may have remained on the island as a castaway. Coconut crabs could have scavenged her remains after her death and carried some bones away from the original location. However, no conclusive evidence establishes that Earhart reached the island or that this was her fate.Why Nikumaroro became central to the theoryNikumaroro lies in the Phoenix Islands of Kiribati, roughly 400 miles southeast of Howland Island, Earhart’s intended destination. Supporters of the castaway hypothesis point to reports of radio signals received after the aircraft disappeared, objects found on the island and the discovery of human bones in 1940. British colonial officials found 13 bones, including a skull. Gerald Gallagher, the island’s administrator, reported that coconut crabs had scattered bones at the discovery site and suggested that the remains might possibly belong to Earhart. The bones were sent to Fiji for examination but were subsequently lost, preventing modern DNA testing of the original remains. Their identity has never been conclusively established.How giant coconut crabs could have scattered her remainsCoconut crabs, scientifically known as Birgus latro, are the world’s largest land-dwelling arthropods. They can measure up to three feet across and weigh more than nine pounds. Their powerful claws help them handle food, while their keen sense of smell allows them to locate potential food sources, including animal remains. Their diet includes fruit, coconuts and animal matter. These scavenging habits form the basis of the theory about Earhart’s possible fate. If she died on Nikumaroro, the crabs might have consumed soft tissue and moved some bones away from the original location, making the remains difficult to recover.What carcass experiments revealedResearchers associated with the International Group for Historic Aircraft Recovery (TIGHAR) investigated whether crabs could help explain the scattered remains. In 2001, the group conducted an experiment on Nikumaroro using a lamb shoulder after an attempt to obtain a pig for the study fell through. Its account describes how hermit crabs and young coconut crabs appeared to remove flesh and disperse some bones, although the researchers did not directly observe every part of the process. A later experiment involving a pig carcass was described by National Geographic. The report said coconut crabs and smaller strawberry hermit crabs gathered around the body, removed much of its flesh within two weeks and were associated with bones being moved as far as 60 feet from the original location.A new expedition investigates a mysterious objectIn October 2026, a 17-member expedition backed by Purdue University, the Purdue Research Foundation and the Archaeological Legacy Institute reached Nikumaroro to investigate an underwater feature known as the Taraia Object. The team travelled approximately 830 nautical miles over five days to reach the remote atoll.The object was noticed in satellite imagery in 2020 and appears to have a shape that some observers believe resembles aircraft wreckage. According to Purdue University’s October 14 update, researchers began an underwater survey using a magnetometer and side-scan sonar. The team is examining the feature to determine whether it could be related to Earhart’s missing Lockheed Electra 10-E. The object remains unidentified. Ric Gillespie, a veteran Earhart investigator and executive director of TIGHAR, has argued that the shape is a fallen pandanus tree and its root system rather than aircraft debris. Further examination is needed to establish what the object is and whether it has any connection to Earhart’s aircraft.The October 2026 expedition could provide new evidence about the aircraft and help researchers assess the broader castaway hypothesis. Until the Taraia Object is identified or other evidence directly links Earhart to Nikumaroro, the possibility that she survived a crash landing before dying as a castaway and being scavenged by giant coconut crabs remains unconfirmed.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'All for one man': CJP's Dipke targets Centre for sweeping curbs to stamp out anti-CEC protests
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) activist Abhijeet Dipke on Thursday accused the government of detaining protesters and even opposition leaders that
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) activist Abhijeet Dipke on Thursday accused the government of detaining protesters and even opposition leaders that include former chief ministers, just to save “one man”, chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Addressing the media, Dipke said students, organisations, and the youth protesting for the past 10-15 days were being “dragged away”, while opposition leaders were detained too.“For the past 10-15 days, students’ organisations and the youth of Delhi have been out on the streets, being dragged away. When the Opposition joined them, they were detained too, including the leader of the opposition and former chief ministers like Mamata Banerjee, Arvind Kejriwal and Pinarayi Vijayan,” Dipke said.“All this for whom? For one man, Gyanesh Kumar,” he added.Dipke further alleged that Railways services were suspended after the October 10 call, saying this was possibly the first time such a step had been taken in the country’s history.“That wasn’t enough, so they shut the Metro and closed stations across Delhi. For whom? Gyanesh Kumar. Still not satisfied, they brought in forces from Jammu and Kashmir,” he said.Meanwhile, All India Students' Association leader and activist, Neha Bora, expressed solidarity with the media and criticised the authorities over the detention and alleged harassment of journalists.Speaking at the press conference, Bora said journalists were detained for hours and even beaten, despite having their press cards.“We saw how cameras were snatched from journalists and they were told that they would not get the camera if they cover this,” she said.Bora accused the police of backing a particular political party and of cracking down on the public instead of maintaining law and order.Meanwhile, the CJP and other organisations have called on people to wave the national flag at Central Park in Delhi’s Connaught Place on Saturday.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Hawaii's Hā‘ena State Park closed on Sept 6 as Hurricane Lowell approached; 39 days later, it reopened after repairs, but overnight camping and hiking past two miles remain closed
articles.summary: Hā‘ena State Park on the Hawaiian island of Kaua‘i reopened to visitors on October 15, 39 days after it was closed ahead of Hurricane Lowell.
articles.body: Hā‘ena State Park on the Hawaiian island of Kaua‘i reopened to visitors on October 15, 39 days after it was closed ahead of Hurricane Lowell. While visitors can return to the park and resume some day hikes, overnight camping and hiking beyond the first two miles of the Kalalau Trail remain prohibited until further notice. According to the Hawaii Department of Land and Natural Resources (DLNR), the park was closed on September 6 because of safety concerns as Hurricane Lowell approached. The closure was extended to allow staff to assess hazards and complete repairs before allowing visitors back.The reopening brings back access to one of Kaua‘i’s popular coastal destinations, but restrictions remain in place as recovery work continues across the island’s state parks.What visitors can access after the reopeningAccording to the DLNR announcement published on October 13, Hā‘ena State Park will be open daily from 7 am to 6:45 pm, including holidays, unless an emergency closure is announced. Shuttle services to the park also resumed on October 15. Visitors can once again undertake day-use hikes to Hanakāpīʻai Beach and Valley, as well as Hanakāpīʻai Falls. However, two restrictions remain. Overnight camping is closed, and hikers cannot continue beyond the two-mile point along the Kalalau Trail. Both restrictions will remain in place until further notice.The Kalalau Trail is an 11-mile route along Kaua‘i’s Nāpali Coast. The park also provides access to Kē‘ē Beach and the trail leading towards Hanakāpīʻai Beach and Falls. Visitors planning a trip should check the official park conditions page before travelling.Park staff removed damaged trees before reopeningThe closure was extended beyond the initial safety shutdown to give park personnel time to inspect hazards and carry out repairs. In its October 13 announcement, DLNR State Parks Administrator Alan Carpenter credited park staff and community partners Hui Makaʻāinana o Makana and the Hanalei Initiative with helping restore access. “Park staff and our partners Hui Makaʻāinana o Makana and the Hanalei Initiative worked diligently to get this iconic state park and trail back open for public use following this devastating storm,” Carpenter said. The department said the decision to reopen was made in consultation with community leaders, balancing public safety and the needs of the local community.Around 50 local jobs depend on the parkThe reopening also has an economic dimension. According to Carpenter, Hā‘ena State Park supports about 50 local jobs. He noted that the community had previously experienced a much longer closure after severe flooding in 2018, when Hā‘ena State Park and Nāpali Coast State Wilderness Park were shut from April 2018 to June 2019. The 2026 reopening, he said, followed a careful and collaborative decision with community leaders.Entry fees and reservations for visitorsThe DLNR has also clarified the entry rules for residents and visitors from outside Hawaii.Hawaii residents: Entry is free with a Hawaii driver's licence or state-issued identification. Residents do not need reservations for day passes. Thirty parking spaces are reserved for residents, and everyone in the vehicle must show Hawaii identification.Visitors from outside Hawaii: Advance reservations are required through the Go Hā‘ena website.Entrance fee: $5 per person for out-of-state visitors. Children aged three and under enter free.Parking: Out-of-state parking reservations cost $10 per vehicle.Visitors should confirm availability and access conditions before setting out, particularly if they intend to hike beyond the sections that have reopened.Other Kaua‘i parks remain closed or restrictedHā‘ena is not the only park affected by storm-related disruption. In its October 13 update, DLNR said Kōke‘e and Waimea Canyon state parks would remain closed until further notice because of extensive damage. Other Kaua‘i state parks also remained closed to visitation and camping, subject to the department's latest notices. At Wailua River State Park, access to the river, designated landing area and trailhead is permitted, but individual kayakers cannot enter Fern Grotto. Hiking beyond the trailhead remains prohibited, and access to Uluwehi Falls, also known as Secret Falls, is still closed.The department said refunds would be credited to visitors who missed park days, camping or lodging because of storm-related closures. Refund processing may take two to three weeks. The reopening of Hā‘ena State Park restores access to its beaches and some hiking routes, but it does not mean every trail or camping area is ready for use. Visitors should follow the remaining restrictions and consult official notices for changes.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Beyond reels: 3 influencers, 3 killings, a trail of questions
articles.summary: CHANDIGARH: A video can make someone famous overnight. A controversial opinion can turn them into a target.
articles.body: CHANDIGARH: A video can make someone famous overnight. A controversial opinion can turn them into a target. And in the world of social media, where every post is open to public scrutiny, the line between criticism and hostility can become dangerously blurred.For content creators, the internet is more than a platform to entertain. It is also a space to express themselves, build an identity and earn a living. But not everyone who watches their content agrees with what they see. Some respond with criticism, others with abuse and threats.The more disturbing question is what happens when disapproval moves beyond the screen.In Punjab, the deaths of social media creators Mad Sandhu, Kanchan Kumari and Manjeet Kaur have brought renewed attention to three separate murder cases involving influencers with lakhs of followers.One was found strangled inside a car. Another was allegedly abducted, taken to an isolated area and set on fire. The third was shot dead outside a car-washing facility.Kanchan Kumari, popularly known as Kamal Kaur ‘Bhabhi’, had nearly four lakh Instagram followers. Manjeet Kaur had built an audience of around 1.46 lakh, while Amritsar-based make-up artist Madhusudan Singh, known online as Mad Sandhu, had around 2.26 lakh followers.Their content and audiences differed, as did the circumstances of their deaths. Here is a look at the three cases and what investigators have established so far.Mad Sandhu: Shot dead outside car-washing facilityMad Sandhu, whose real name was Madhusudan Singh, was shot dead on Loharka Road in Amritsar on October 3, 2026.The make-up artist, who had more than two lakh Instagram followers, had spoken openly about gender and LGBTQ+ issues.He had also faced objections to his clothing, older videos and social media activity from a Nihang group months before his death. Sandhu had said he had changed and that old clips were being recirculated.Several suspects were arrested, including Jobanpreet, a key accused apprehended in Mumbai on October 14. Police said he allegedly played a role in the movement of weapons and logistical support for the shooters.However, investigators have not publicly established a conclusive motive for Sandhu’s murder.Manjeet Kaur: Abducted and set on firePunjabi social media influencer and YouTuber Manjeet Kaur died at PGIMER in Chandigarh on August 26, 2026, after suffering severe burn injuries. She had shared lifestyle videos, beauty product promotions and family vlogs.According to her mother’s complaint, two acquaintances called Manjeet to Chandigarh’s Sector 34 on the intervening night of July 3 and 4.She was allegedly forced into a vehicle and taken to a wooded area near Morinda, where she was tied to a tree and set on fire.A passerby reportedly helped extinguish the flames before she was taken for treatment. She remained under medical care for nearly two months before succumbing to her injuries.The case also raised questions about an alleged delay in recording her statement. Reports said Manjeet had expressed a desire to give a statement while she was conscious during treatment, but the investigating officer allegedly did not reach the hospital.Punjab Police denied negligence, saying the alleged abduction had taken place in Chandigarh and fell under Chandigarh Police’s jurisdiction.Following her death, Chandigarh Police registered a murder case.Investigators have been examining the alleged abduction, the roles of those named in the complaint and the motive behind the attack. No confirmed link between Manjeet’s social media content and her killing has emerged in the reported investigation.Kanchan Kumari: Found strangled inside a carThe sequence of cases dates back to June 2025, when social media creator Kanchan Kumari, popularly known as Kamal Kaur ‘Bhabhi’, was found dead inside a car parked near Adesh Medical University in Bathinda.Kanchan, who was from Ludhiana, had left for a promotional video shoot. Her body was found in the vehicle on June 11, 2025. A postmortem examination confirmed that she had died of strangulation.Police alleged that the killing was linked to objections raised by the accused to videos she posted online. Amritpal Singh Mehron, identified as the main accused, had allegedly objected to content he considered vulgar and to her use of the name ‘Kaur’.Police described the murder as an instance of “moral policing”.Mehron fled to the UAE after the crime and was brought back to India in April 2026. Other accused were also arrested, and police filed a supplementary chargesheet against Mehron and another accused in May 2026.A Bathinda court framed murder charges against Mehron and an associate in August 2026.Three murders in 16 monthsIn a span of around 16 months, three social media creators with lakhs of followers were murdered in Punjab. The circumstances differed: Kanchan was strangled, Manjeet died after an alleged abduction and arson attack, and Sandhu was shot dead in public.The three cases have placed the deaths of public-facing social media creators at the centre of separate murder investigations in Punjab. While the evidence and circumstances differ, all three involved people who had built sizable audiences online and whose killings have left investigators with questions to answer.Public life often demands safety and security, with constant online presence inviting online bullying.Vaishnavi Rampurkar, a Pune resident, said she felt uneasy while reading the comment sections of posts by women influencers and creators from the LGBTQ+ community.“An influencer’s life seems eye-catching, but whenever I scroll through the comments, one question always hits me: is it worth receiving this much hate just because I am following my passion?” she said.Geeta Mamde, a resident of Keshav Nagar area of Pune, spoke about the vulnerability that can accompany pursuing one’s passion in public.“It’s scary how you can be out there pursuing your passion, simply walking or recording a video, and the next moment, your life is taken away. It makes you question how safe we really are,” she added.The three cases involve different circumstances and investigative leads, but each has drawn attention to the vulnerability of people with a public presence. As investigations continue, a key question remains: where does public scrutiny end, and the safety of those living their lives in the public eye begin?You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chandigarh | Silver Rate in Chandigarh | Bank Holidays in Chandigarh | Public Holidays in Chandigarh | Chandigarh AQI | Weather in Chandigarh | Petrol Price in Chandigarh | Diesel Price in Chandigarh | CNG Price in Chandigarh | LPG Price in ChandigarhStay updated with the latest Chandigarh news.
